name: Finnbheara

attributes.attribute: wrote of him in plays and poems

sources: Wilde, Lady. Ancient Legends, Mystic Charms and Superstitions of Ireland. London: Chatto and Windus, 1902, 43.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Finnbheara is an Irish hero, known also as Finvarra, Fin Varra, Fionvarra, and Finbar. People usually said a queen ruled fairyland, but Finnbheara proved to be the exception. He held court in a fairy mound located at Knockma, near Tuam in county Galway, where he governed the fairies of Connacht. Some said he ruled every fairy in Ireland. His wife was the fairy Una. Finnbheara made a habit of stealing lovely women, drawing them close with gentle fairy music. Inside his palace those women set aside their mortal lives, dancing and singing free of sorrow. In the tale told of Eithne the Fair, her body stayed behind in a waking trance, and in others she vanished without a trace. Lady Gregory collected stories of him, and William Butler Yeats wrote of him in several plays and many poems. He came to stand for the beautiful Otherworld.
